## Natural history notes

A medium-sized dove characterized by its pale gray-buff body, long squared tail, black half-collar on the back of the neck, and dark bill. In Florida, it is common in towns, suburbs, farms, parks, roadsides, parking lots, and other open human-associated habitats with scattered trees, wires, or buildings for perching and nesting. It feeds mainly on seeds and grains, usually foraging on the ground in pairs or small flocks, and is often seen around feeders, agricultural areas, and urban landscapes.
